I want to cancel it because my plans changed, but before you do anything, confirm whether the whole trip is eligible for cancellation and give me the full itinerary, both passengers on the booking, any insurance attached, the total baggage count, the payment method used, and exactly how the refund would work.
summary: Maya asks the agent to run a multi-booking session: pull up and cancel round-trip C4C633, review and cancel the earlier one-way EC4C1C, change A2CBB0 to the cheapest nearby flight, and book two new one-way trips — all on the same card. The run splits into an opening cancellation block (T1–T2), an EC4C1C review with an insurance self-correction (T3–T4), the A2CBB0 change (T5–T7), and two new bookings plus a recap (T8–T13). The recall traps land on T2, T5, T6, T10, where the agent reliably reads earlier-established facts — reservation IDs, the Mastercard-9834 payment method, passenger details, and the cheapest-flight search result — out of working memory with no re-retrieval. T4 is the densest cognitive turn: the agent inspects the DB insurance-parsing logic and explicitly corrects its own earlier statement, a genuine REFLECT+FIX move (though not itself a probe turn). Memory handling is strong throughout; the one miss is on T2, where the agent recalls C4C633 and the card but does not fully restate the original-card id / 5–7-business-day refund timeframe, so that sub-check fails. Overall it is a clean recall-and-apply run, consistent with the normal-scenario pattern where injected back-references pin the exact params.

findings.title: Recall concentrates on the probe turns
findings.body: All four trap turns (T2/T5/T6/T10) carry a Memory › Read from working memory tag — the agent surfaces reservation IDs, the shared Mastercard, passenger details, and the cheapest-flight result from earlier turns without firing a single retrieval component.

findings.title: The richest turn is a non-probe self-correction
findings.body: T4 fires Reasoning › Analyse source code, Reflection › Self-Correct Step Implementation, and Memory › Read from working memory in one paragraph — the agent re-reads its own scratchpad and overturns an earlier insurance claim, the only true error-recovery move in the run.

findings.title: COMPLY dominates the lens
findings.body: Every probe turn resolves to COMPLY: the normal-scenario back-references are consistent with state the agent already holds, so recall-and-apply never conflicts with reflection — the sole sub-check failure (T2 refund timeframe) is an incompleteness, not a memory contradiction.
